extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, animal breeders and horsemen (readers of a medieval/early-modern natural-history treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: A section of a natural-history treatise giving practical criteria for judging the quality, health, temper, and gaits of horses (how to inspect head, neck, body, legs, hooves, color, appetite, and movement; how to test obedience and spirit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Head and neck conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Caput parvum, erectum; oculis vivacibus; auribus parvis; collo brevi, recto, et rectis comis decora (Latin phrasing in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the head first when presenting the horse: small, well-set head; lively, bright eyes; small ears; short, erect and not-weak neck (collo brevi, recto). These features indicate good temperament and suitability for riding. The author emphasizes examining the head before other parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chest width and forepart
rubrics_metrics.description: Pecore lato; parte anteriore sublimiore parum (broad chest, neither too small nor excessively narrow in forequarters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad chest (pecore lato) is desirable. Forequarters should not be too small relative to the body; balance between fore and hind parts is important for strength and locomotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back, spine and loins (absence of scars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tergo recte rigente, in quo nulla sint cicatricum vestigia; lumbi pleni (straight back, no traces of scars, full loins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the back and loins for straightness and soundness; absence of scars or deformities (vestigia cicatricum) indicates the horse has not suffered disabling injuries. Full loins (lumbi pleni) signal strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tail carriage and condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Cauda pulchra; cauda recta, non incedit aut intus se collidentibus aut extrà deflexis (beautiful tail, carried properly and not clashing between thighs or deflected outward).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the tail: if the tail drags or the horse carries it improperly (e.g., tucked, deflected, or clashing between the thighs) this signifies weakness (if tail is dragged it indicates imbecility). A well-set, handsome tail is a positive sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legs, joints and hoof conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pede lato & ungula crassiore; juncturas firmas breuibas; ungulas duras, coriis duris (wide feet, thick/strong hooves; firm and short limb joints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check limb joints and hooves: wide feet and thick hooves are prized; joints should be firm and short rather than spindly. Hard, durable hoof horn and tough skin (corii duri) are indicators of durability and suitability for bearing weight and traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry and absence of blemishes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nulla sint cicatricum vestigia; partes rectae et firmæ; pares maculas fugiunt; impares probant (absence of scars, symmetry of parts; evenness of markings preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetry of body parts and lack of scarred or distorted areas are desirable. The author notes that even (symmetrical) markings and features are preferred; asymmetry (in legs, markings) is looked upon less favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and facial/leg markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Colorem considera; stellam candidam in fronte laudatur; si maculae sunt paribus (consider color; a white star on the forehead is praised; some markings on all or both forelegs may be thought better).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess coat color and markings: a bright, lustrous coat is praised. Specific small white markings (e.g., a white star on the forehead) are commended; the treatise gives nuanced preference for certain patterns but cautions that overall lustre (nitor) is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breathing and throat (guttural) test
rubrics_metrics.description: Guttur comprime; si anhelitu fit haud integro (compress the throat and judge breathing; panting indicates unsoundness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use breathing and throat tests to detect weakness or respiratory problems: if the horse pants or its breathing indicates an insecure chest/respiration, it is not sound. The throat and wind are diagnostic of fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age indicators (joints and throat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect joints (iun&uras singulas maxime iuxta pedes) and throat/gullet to infer age: certain compressions and looseness indicate youth or senescence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the joints near the feet and the throat region to estimate age and vigor—young animals have particular joint characteristics; weakness or distension in these regions suggests morbidity or advanced age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appetite and feeding behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Si alacriter edit, bonus; si segniter, vel iners est vel gulofus; absumpta auena si recumbit segnis est (eating briskly is good; slow or indolent eating is a negative sign; a horse that lies down after oats is lazy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how the horse eats: eager and prompt eating indicates good constitution and spirit; sluggish, slow, or gluttonous behavior indicates laziness or poor temperament. Responses to offered oats and how the horse handles grain are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction to bit, bridle and saddle (obedience and spirit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fac currere, videbis cum retinetur quam pareat freno & bit; currendo quantum calcaribus; si frena mandit, spuma edita, spiritus (test obedience under control: response to rein and bit, foaming, spirited behaviour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the animal under tack: observe how it yields to the rein and bit, whether it foams at the mouth when excited, how it responds to spur and bridle. A horse that respects the bit, obeys the rein, and displays correct spiritedness without dangerous obstinacy is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior near water and wheels (courage and steadiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad aquas deducito: agnosces an se volúntarie in aquá latere; ad rotas deducito: si egre accedit, pavidus est, si non vult, obstinatus (lead it to water and wheels to test fear or stubbornness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose the horse to potentially frightening stimuli (water, cart wheels): a well-tempered animal will approach water and wheels appropriately; reluctance indicates stubbornness or timidity. Also observe whether it will enter or swim when required—useful for gauging trainability and courage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gait quality: stride, synchronization, and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Celeritatis inceffus causa: (1) crura moueant velociter, (2) duos simul moueat pedes non unum, (3) pedes multum spatij amplectantur; distinctions of simple, velitatione, gradarius, propaflus, tortorí (criteria for speed: rapid leg movement, paired leg motion, long stride; the treatise defines multiple gait types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe movement to assess speed and safety: speed arises from rapid limb action, coordinated paired-motions (two legs moved together rather than single alternating), and long stride where hind-foot placement extends beyond fore. The text characterizes many gaits—simple (slow), velitatione, gradarius (two-same-side legs move together producing speed and lesser fatigue), propaflus, tortorí, etc.—and explains how to distinguish them by which feet move and timing. Test by making the horse run and note leg sequencing, how much it yields to the bridle while moving, and its steadiness; these observations indicate suitability for racing, bearing, or riding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-appropriate virtues: lightness, speed, and endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Leuis, quàm velox, quàm tutus, quamque spiritu gravi aut facili: (assess how light, fast, safe, and full-breathed the horse is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different equine roles require different balances: a good riding horse should be light, fast, safe, and display adequate lung capacity; evaluate by observing running, response to spur, and ease of motion. The combination of alacrity (alacritas), lack of excessive sweating in labor, and steadiness are signs of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainability and memory under danger
rubrics_metrics.description: If the horse, after a near-suffocation (immersio) or severe aversive training, avoids repeating the dangerous action, it is corrigible; if not, use alternative handling (e.g., restraining head) (text gives training examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise recommends practical training tests: a horse that voluntarily learns from a severe but non-fatal aversive (e.g., near-drowning) will avoid repeating the dangerous act and is more easily corrected. A horse that resists and will not progress despite restraint is problematic; the method of correction (immersio, dragging, controlling head) is discussed as diagnostics of teachability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response when saddled and in harness (soundness under load)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructed with bridle and harness: if when saddled it neighs, foams, moves willingly, bears the rider, and does not show lameness or unwillingness to go, it is fit for service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the horse under rider or harness for willingness to move, capacity to be restrained and controlled without excessive kicking or refusal, and continued soundness (no lameness or pain). Sudden reluctance under load, refusal to move forward, or signs of pain indicate unsuitability for riding or draught work.
